bug_semantics: An attacker-controlled Typebot imported from JSON could retain a Script block whose content the preview API returned as a client-side action. @typebot.io/js then compiled that untrusted content with Function/AsyncFunction directly in the authenticated builder page. Code run there could make same-origin fetch requests with the victim's session, enumerate the victim's user/workspace credentials, receive decrypted credential data from credentials.getCredentials, and exfiltrate API keys, OAuth tokens, and passwords. The workspace form of getCredentials also authorized the supplied workspace but, at the vulnerable snapshot, did not bind the requested credential ID to that workspace.
flaw_origin: The single member commit behind PR #194 introduced all three causal pieces together: file import accepted JSON.parse(fileContent) without marking executable blocks untrusted, the viewer converted Script/Code block content into a codeToExecute client action, and the new @typebot.io/js executeCode implementation invoked Function on that content in the page context. It supplied neither a trust boundary for imported bots nor a sandbox/credentialless execution context.
ai_marker: absent — the BIC commit object names human author and committer Baptiste Arnaud <contact@baptiste-arnaud.fr>; its complete message is ':alembic: Implement bot v2 MVP' followed by 'Closes #190', with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI, bot, or other automation trailer/marker.
evidence: The first-party GHSA bundle identifies packages/embeds/js/src/features/blocks/logic/script/executeScript.ts, describes arbitrary client-side script execution with the victim's authenticated session and plaintext credential retrieval, declares @typebot.io/js < 0.9.15 affected / 0.9.15 first patched, and references https://github.com/baptisteArno/typebot.io/commit/a68f0c91790af8f52f17557f4aa202e966e7e579.

`git log -L 6,17:packages/embeds/js/src/features/blocks/logic/script/executeScript.ts a5cf298cc8043e95c6988779be8c9e0e495e0378` follows the vulnerable Function/AsyncFunction execution through formatting, renames, and refactors to its creation in landed commit 1a3869ae6d9fa92fc71ef9d981bfffb8e4ee4ecc; the 2023 rename a842f572974123884b67ac4c01d4c6d09abe08a8 and later changes did not originate the execution mechanism.

GitHub PR #194's first-party commits endpoint (`gh api repos/baptisteArno/typebot.io/pulls/194/commits`) returns exactly one member, 3487850b9f4808617d347ddde4d9701f56662894, parent e55823e0112291a32886908fd4c63365275106e6. `git rev-parse` shows that member and landed squash 1a3869ae6d9fa92fc71ef9d981bfffb8e4ee4ecc have the same tree 1c7360226886e227373c9affe2a374c1fbe7c750 and the same parent, so the member is a losslessly reconstructed smallest BIC rather than the squash wrapper.

At 3487850b9f4808617d347ddde4d9701f56662894, apps/builder/src/features/templates/components/ImportTypebotFromFileButton.tsx passes JSON.parse(fileContent) directly to onNewTypebot; apps/viewer/src/features/blocks/logic/code/api/utils/executeCode.ts places block.options.content and arguments into logic.codeToExecute; and packages/js/src/features/blocks/logic/code/utils/executeCode.ts constructs `Function(...args.map((arg) => arg.id), content)` and invokes it. These are the imported-payload, dispatch, and authenticated-page execution links required by the advisory attack path.

Immediate-parent tree verification is direct: `git ls-tree -r --name-only e55823e0112291a32886908fd4c63365275106e6 -- packages/js/src/features/blocks/logic/code/utils/executeCode.ts` returns no path, while the same command at 3487850b9f4808617d347ddde4d9701f56662894 returns that file. The parent also predates the new packages/js package and PR #194's import/dispatch implementation; thus the vulnerable @typebot.io/js mechanism is absent from the immediate parent.

Release-boundary verification: `git tag --contains 1a3869ae6d9fa92fc71ef9d981bfffb8e4ee4ecc` includes js-v0.0.1 through js-v0.9.14, and `git show js-v0.0.1:packages/js/package.json` reports @typebot.io/js version 0.0.1. The reconstructed member's identical landed tree therefore precedes the affected package line.

The direct fix a68f0c91790af8f52f17557f4aa202e966e7e579 marks imported Script/Set Variable blocks isUnsafe, propagates preview context, and runs unsafe preview code in a Web Worker whose fetch forces credentials: 'omit' and whose cookie-carrying APIs are disabled, instead of the authenticated window's AsyncFunction. The same commit changes packages/embeds/js/package.json from 0.9.14 to 0.9.15.

`git log js-v0.9.14..js-v0.9.15 --` over the executor, importer, and package manifest yields a68f0c91790af8f52f17557f4aa202e966e7e579, and `git tag --contains a68f0c91790af8f52f17557f4aa202e966e7e579 'js-v0.9.*'` begins at js-v0.9.15 and excludes js-v0.9.14, exactly matching the advisory boundary.

`git cat-file -p 3487850b9f4808617d347ddde4d9701f56662894` is the sole AI-attribution source used: it records Baptiste Arnaud as both author and committer and has only the two-line human commit message, with no AI/co-author/generated trailer.
reasoning: The vulnerability is not merely that Typebot intentionally supports scripts; it is a missing trust transition. PR #194 made imported JSON executable in the authenticated preview origin by carrying block content through codeToExecute to a raw Function call. That gives an imported attacker's code the victim's builder origin and session, from which the credential-list/get endpoints provide the confidentiality impact described by the GHSA. Line history proves later AsyncFunction conversion, renames, and refactors preserved the same unsandboxed mechanism. PR #194 was squash-merged, so treating landed 1a3869ae6d9fa92fc71ef9d981bfffb8e4ee4ecc as irreducible would be wrong; the public PR exposes one original member, 3487850b9f4808617d347ddde4d9701f56662894, whose tree and parent exactly equal the landed squash tree and parent. That member is therefore the smallest reconstructable BIC. Its immediate parent has no packages/js executor path, while the BIC creates the importer, server dispatch, and Function sink together. The identical landed tree is present before the first @typebot.io/js release and remains in 0.9.14. Fix a68f0c91790af8f52f17557f4aa202e966e7e579 directly establishes an imported-code trust flag and a credentialless worker for preview, and it is the sole relevant boundary commit between js-v0.9.14 and js-v0.9.15. Finally, the BIC commit object contains only human Baptiste Arnaud authorship/committer identity and no AI marker, so under BIC-only attribution the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
